pool.text: Christopher Columbus named the island of Guanahani, Bahamas San Salvador.
The conquistador Gonzalo de Alvarado founded a mission he named San Salvador.
The city became the seat of the Intendancy of San Salvador.
El Salvador became an independent state after the insurgency against Mexican rule.
San Salvador suffered from many severe earthquakes, the most disastrous of which occurred.
The Museo Nacional de Antropologia was founded by David Joaquin Guzman.
President Arturo Araujo was ousted by a military coup d'etat.
San Salvador hosted the Central American and Caribbean Games.
Celebrations in the Estadio Cuscatlan were held in honor of returning troops.
The San Salvador earthquake destroyed many government buildings and other important structures.
The Chapultepec Peace Accords were signed, ending 12 years of civil war.
The cathedral was inaugurated with a festive tiled ceramic mural facade.
San Salvador adopted the dollar as its currency of exchange.
MARTE, a private nonprofit art organization, opened.
The National Railways of El Salvador resumed railway service.
Mayor Norman Quijano worked to redevelop parks and historic buildings.
Tropical storm Agatha hit the Central American coast.
The Union of Ibero-American Capital Cities selected San Salvador as a capital of culture.
SITRAMS commenced operation to resolve many transportation problems.
Mayor Nayib Bukele presented the redesigned city shield and flag.
